mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates people are spending less time at home, freeing up time and inclination for out-of-home activities, which will translate into higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility continuing its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The recent sharp decline in PARKS mobility suggests a shift away from outdoor leisure, potentially due to weather or event changes, redirecting consumer activity towards indoor retail and recreation, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks, and PARKS mobility continues to decline or remains low.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL mobility suggests people are neither at work nor home, indicating a temporary shift in activity patterns that will eventually re-allocate to RETAIL_REC as routines stabilize, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls while WORKPLACES also dips
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, even if WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL continue to show concurrent declines.

mechanism_narrative: As early summer progresses, the initial surge in PARKS mobility stabilizes or declines, leading to a seasonal redirection of leisure time and spending towards indoor or less weather-dependent retail and recreation activities, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility continues to rise significantly over the next four weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not show an improvement.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent recovery in TRANSIT mobility over the past three weeks, despite a recent plateau, signals a broader return to out-of-home activities and commuting, which will drive increased footfall and spending in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility declines or remains stagnant below -22.0 for more than two consecutive weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not improve.

mechanism_narrative: The recent week-on-week dip in RETAIL_REC is a temporary fluctuation; a quick rebound above the t-1w level signals renewed consumer confidence and a continuation of the recovery trend, leading to higher RETAIL_REC in the immediate next week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 points week-on-week from t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase by more than 2 points week-on-week from t-0w, or it continues to decline in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates reduced time spent on essential local errands and at home, suggesting a shift towards more discretionary out-of-home activities, which will benefit RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both show a week-on-week decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat over the next two weeks, despite both GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL showing continued week-on-week declines.

mechanism_narrative: The recent dip in WORKPLACES mobility, if sustained, indicates a stalled return-to-office trend, reducing weekday foot traffic in central business districts and urban centers, which will negatively impact overall RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -18.0 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility recovers significantly above -16.0 within the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days.
